title: Microburst admission control simulation notes
body:
Context and quick intent:
- scribbling a small sim to reason about microbursts (short, high-rate spikes) and how admission control + batching/backpressure interact with latency SLOs and token cost.
- trying to get away from purely token-bucket thinking; want a hybrid that understands short correlation windows and sequence-length coupling.

Goals:
- model: small event-driven simulator for a worker pool + request queue + batching engine + KV cache hit variance.
- evaluate: 95th/99th latency tail under different admission policies and burst budgets; token cost per 1k requests; percent of requests served with cold-kv misses.
- outcome: propose a lightweight runtime admission config (3 params) and a corresponding client-side backoff hint surface.

Hypothesis (rough):
- a short-lived microburst detector (window = 250ms) + ephemeral per-tenant burst budget reduces 99p latency more effectively than aggressive global rate limits because it permits short tolerated bursts without starving steady traffic.
- coupling budget decay to EWMA of interarrival variance avoids long tail starvation after burst drain.

Workload shapes to test (synthetic):
1) steady-steady: Poisson lambda=20 rps, seq_len ~Geom(p=0.2) mean ~5 tokens
2) microburst-on-steady: baseline Poisson 10 rps + every 10s a 400ms burst with peak 600 rps (triangular ramp up/down), seq_len bimodal (90% short, 10% long)
3) correlated-requests: bursts where consecutive requests are long (mean seq_len 120) to stress KV and memory pressure
4) sawtooth / diurnal: low-high cycles over 60s windows to test longer-lived allocations

Key sim components (simplified):
- Ingress stream: emit arrival timestamps + tenant_id + seq_len
- Burst detector: sliding window counts W (ms). compute instantaneous rate r = counts / W. maintain EWMA sigma of interarrival variance. if r > threshold(tenant) => microburst flag.
- Burst budget: per-tenant float B, max_B = config.burst_capacity; on microburst start, allow usage from B; B decays with half_life param when idle. replenishes slowly when steady usage low.
- Admission policy: if queue_depth > q_high => reject/soft-defer; if using budget => allow even if q_high until budget exhausted; otherwise prefer short requests (heuristic: estimate expected service_time(seq_len)).
- Batching engine: continuous batching with max_batch_tokens and max_latency_ms. batching increases throughput at cost of tail for small-arrival rates.
- Workers: per-GPU slots with avg service_time = model_token_time * seq_len + kernel_overhead + kv_miss_penalty (prob based on seq history).

Config knobs I want in runtime YAML (candidate):
runtime_admission:
  burst_capacity_tokens: 100000    # tenant-level ephemeral allowance (token units)
  burst_window_ms: 250            # detection window for microburst
  burst_half_life_sec: 20         # budget decay (seconds)
  prefer_short_requests: true     # heuristic to keep tail down
  q_high_threshold: 64            # queue length to trigger strict throttling
  client_hint_ttl_ms: 500         # how long backpressure hints remain valid

Pseudocode of decision flow (notes-to-self):
- on_request(r):
    tenant = r.tenant
    append to ingress_ringbuffer(tenant, now)
    compute r = sliding_rate(tenant, burst_window_ms)
    if r > tenant.rate_threshold:
      set microburst=true
    if queue_len >= q_high_threshold and tenant.burst_budget <= 0:
      return HTTP 429 + hint(backoff_ms = compute_backoff(...))
    else if microburst and tenant.burst_budget > 0:
      allocate tokens = min(seq_len, tenant.burst_budget)
      tenant.burst_budget -= tokens
      enqueue(request)
    else:
      enqueue(request)

- background_tick(dt):
    for each tenant:
      tenant.burst_budget += replenish_rate * dt  (cap at max_B)
      tenant.burst_budget *= 2^{-dt / half_life_sec}  (decay model when idle)

Backpressure hint idea (client-facing):
- when we 429/503, include header X-RW-Backoff: delta_ms=250; token_budget_left=12345; estimated_wait_ms=200.
- client-side: soft-gateway can queue for up to hint. Also use header to adapt retry jitter.

Metrics (telemetry) to emit per-tenant/per-route:
- microburst_count (per-window)
- burst_budget_used (tokens/sec), burst_budget_remaining
- admitted_during_burst_pct
- q_len_histogram, batch_size_histogram, worker_busy_pct
- tail_latency_50/95/99
- kv_miss_rate and kv_miss_cost_ms

Simulation measurement plan:
- baseline: no burst budget, global RB token-bucket rate limit tuned to 150% baseline throughput.
- config grid: burst_capacity_tokens in [0, 1e4, 1e5, 5e5]; burst_half_life [5s, 20s, 60s]; burst_window [100ms, 250ms, 500ms]; prefer_short_requests [true,false].
- run 50 replicates per combination for each workload shape. record tail stats and cost proxy (GPU-ms).

Edge cases / things I still worry about:
- multi-tenant resource contention: if many tenants burst simultaneously we need a cluster-level policy (global emergency cap) to avoid OOM. But local budgets could mask overload until it's too late.
- adversarial clients gaming burst budget by splitting requests across many tenant ids. Need per-identity coupling (client_id vs tenant_id).
- prefer_short_requests heuristic could starve legitimate long jobs and increase overall cost if long tails accumulate. Need fair-share fallback.
- KV miss cascades: bursts of cold long requests will amplify latency nonlinearly. Simulation should model cache TTL + prewarm probability when sequential bursts seen.

Quick simulation implementation notes (py-ish):
- event loop: heapq of (time, event). inflow generator emits arrival events. workers consume enqueued requests when free. batching logic check on enqueue + periodic flush timers.
- keep per-tenant small state struct: {budget, arrivals_ring, ewma_var, last_activity}
- run with seed+determinism and dump traces for worst runs.

Experiment outputs I want to plot:
- time series of queue depth, batch sizes, admitted rate vs arrival rate (zoomed around bursts)
- scatter of seq_len vs latency at 99th for admitted vs rejected
- heatmap of config grid -> 99p latency / token-cost ratio

Next steps (immediate):
- implement minimal sim harness (2 days): fixed worker pool, simple model time per token = 0.8ms, kv_miss_penalty = 40ms (miss prob depends on recency), batching: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_latency_ms=10.
- run first experiments on microburst-on-steady workload and iterate on heuristics.
- sync with Marcus + SRE to discuss global emergency cap idea.

Notes-to-self (random quick brainstorm):
- consider hybrid budget unit: tokens + request-slots. tokens handle long sequences, slots handle pure arrival volume.
- maybe incorporate predictive prewarm: if we detect burst pattern repeating every 10s, kick async prewarm for next window (cost tradeoff).
- test with real traces (sampled from production ingress) once sim is stable.

Open questions to decide in design doc later:
- what should default burst_capacity_tokens be for new tenants? conservative value vs adaptive bootstrap.
- whether client hints should be opt-in (privacy) or always present (useful for better UX).
- do we expose per-tenant budget as a metric in the Console? (iffy, could be abused)

End-of-file.
